If your app keeps all of its state in a store such as Redux or MobX, state inside a component is a second place where data lives, and the store doesn't know about it. This rule reports every call to `this.setState` in a class component or a `createReactClass` component.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"react/no-set-state" = "error" # or "warn"
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```jsx
class Counter extends React.Component {
  increment() {
    this.setState({ count: this.state.count + 1 });
  }

  render() {
    return <button onClick={() => this.increment()}>{this.state.count}</button>;
  }
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```jsx
class Counter extends React.Component {
  render() {
    return <button onClick={this.props.onIncrement}>{this.props.count}</button>;
  }
}
```

## When not to use it

Local state is a normal part of React. Only turn this rule on if your project has decided to keep all state outside its components. It doesn't look at the `useState` hook.
